Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Winter 2027 Anime season is right around the corner, and with it comes a massive slate of brand-new and returning series coming to global streaming giants. HIDIVE, one of the most popular anime streaming destinations in the world is premiering 2027's biggest new comedy series, Giant Ojosama — also known as Giant Young Lady in English which will officially begin streaming during the Winter 2027 Anime season. Based on the original manga series by Nikumura-Q, Giant Ojosama 's anime adaptation is is directed by Hiroshi Ikehata alongside Yu Sato who will be working on series composition and scripts, character design and chief animation direction from Hajime Mitsuda and animation production by Tatsunoko Production.

In addition to Giant Ojosama coming to HIDIVE as the Winter 2027 season kicks off, HIDIVE will be premiering the new series as part of their special screenings on December 4 at Anime Frontier 2026 in Fort Worth, Texas, to give fans attending the convention a special first look at the new series. For those who will be watching the series from home, HIDIVE will be streaming Giant Ojosama to subscribers in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand in January as a simulcast broadcast.

From HIDIVE, Giant Ojosama follows Oriko Fujido , a young heiress of Fujido Zaibatsu, the world's largest beverage and vending machine company. Oriko was gifted an entire town on her 4th birthday and ever since, she's worked tirelessly to help the town grow alongside her personal butler and researcher Dr. Sebastian. Just as she turns fourteen, the town is suddenly invaded by a giant kaiju. As Oriko declares it's her job to protect the town, Dr. Sebastian creates an experimental energy drink that turns Oriko into a skyscraper-sized giant to fight off the kaiju invader, which ultimately results in her new form creating havoc all around her. The anime adaptation of Giant Ojosama stars Yu Serizawa as Oriko Fujido, Junya Enoki as Dr. Sebastian and Imayanagi Ris as Madoka Ito.

The series was originally penned by Nikumura-Q in 2021, Giant Ojosama is a currently ongoing serialization by Shogakukan and is available through Sunday Web ry, an online platform that's accesible through standard web browsers and a mobile app. As of writing, the series currently has 13-collected volumes and was nominated for the eighth Next Manga Awards in 2022. Additionally, the series ranked 5th place in AnimeJapan's 6th "Most Wanted Anime Adaptation" polls in 2023.

HIDIVE's massive library of anime has made the service the perfect destination for anime fans. After their stacked Fall 2026 lineup , which included highly-anticipated releases like the raunchy rom-com I'm Dating a Dark Summoner , the long-awaited return of Reincarnated as a Sword , the visually stunning Nia Liston: The Merciless Maiden and the absolutely adorable slice-of-life series TetsuRyo , it should come as no surprise that the streaming service would be fully prepared to deliver an even bigger Winter 2027 collection.

While their complete lineup for the upcoming anime season hasn't been announced in full, their upcoming December 4th stream from their showcase panel at Anime Frontier in Texas promises a special first look at Giant Ojosama and other screeners HIDIVE will be presenting to fans. Until then, anime fans can keep a lookout for updates on Giant Ojosama 's global release in January through HIDIVE. Are you going to check out this one when it hits? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: ‘Michael’ Won’t Be Submitted for BAFTA Awards as Filmmakers Pass on Billion-Dollar Biopic’s Entry (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: The highest-grossing biopic ever made is sitting out one of the biggest stops on the road to the Oscars. “Michael,” Antoine Fuqua’s billion-dollar portrait of the King of Pop, will not be submitted for the 2027 EE BAFTA Film Awards, Variety has learned exclusively. That takes actors like Jaafar Jackson and Colman Domingo, along with […]
articles.content:
The highest-grossing biopic ever made is sitting out one of the biggest stops on the road to the Oscars .

“ Michael ,” Antoine Fuqua’s billion-dollar portrait of the King of Pop, will not be submitted for the 2027 EE BAFTA Film Awards, Variety has learned exclusively. That takes actors like Jaafar Jackson and Colman Domingo, along with the film’s entire craft team, out of the running before longlist voting begins. Related Stories Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Russell Crowe Sci-Fi Thriller 'Bluefly' Adds 'Beast' Star Daniel MacPherson (EXCLUSIVE) 'Beast in Me' Season 2 Casts Riley Keough, Lorelei Olivia Mote, Aaron Paul, Taip Ceman, Matthew James Thomas

According to sources with direct knowledge, producer Graham King, Fuqua and various stakeholders made the call after consulting with Lionsgate, international distributor Universal Pictures and the film’s other partners. The sources cite “multiple factors” behind the decision but declined to say what they are. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Representatives for Lionsgate, Universal Pictures and GK Films declined to comment.

Sources tell Variety that Lionsgate supports the filmmakers’ decision.

Earlier this month, the organization sent film voting members its Recommended Viewing Groups for the 2027 awards, which divides every entered film into 15 groups. Each member is randomly assigned one. The British Academy encourages voters to watch as many entries as they can but asks those short on time to prioritize their assigned group and the films in their specialist craft category. “Michael” isn’t in any of them.

BAFTA’s Stage Two entry and deadline passed Nov. 19. A draft list of entered films goes out to entrants and members Nov. 26. The final list will be published on Dec. 4, the same morning Round One voting opens to set the longlists.

Among the films that entered are “The Odyssey,” “Artificial,” “Behemoth!,” “Project Hail Mary,” “Wuthering Heights” and “The Social Reckoning.” The year’s other box office heavyweights, “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” are also in the mix, along with two music documentaries, “Epic: Elvis Presley in Concert” and “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It’s an unusual move for a film that has spent the fall building an awards case.

The 80th BAFTA Film Awards reclaim its traditional spot ahead of the Academy this season. Last year, the British Academy announced nominations five days after the Oscars did, breaking a pattern that had held since 2001. This time, longlists arrive Jan. 7 and nominations Jan. 19, two days before the Academy unveils its own on Jan. 21. The London ceremony follows Feb. 21, three weeks ahead of the March 14 Oscars at the Dolby Theatre. For voters on both sides of the Atlantic, the BAFTA ballot is the first real read on the Oscar race, especially given the Academy’s large international voting bloc.

It’s also a departure from producer King’s own playbook. “Bohemian Rhapsody,” his last music biopic, won Rami Malek the BAFTA for leading actor on the way to four Oscars, which he repeated.

King has criticized the British Academy before . After February’s ceremony, Tourette’s syndrome campaigner John Davidson involuntarily shouted the N-word while “Sinners” stars Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo presented the night’s first award, and the BBC aired the slur despite a two-hour tape delay. Both organizations apologized.

“For years, BAFTA and the BBC have repeatedly displayed cultural insensitivity and tone deafness,” King said at the time in a statement posted to his GK Films’ Instagram account. “Their inability to take accountability for their actions or inactions is reckless and unacceptable.”

The sources did not say whether the episode factored into this year’s decision.

The news also comes after the Golden Globes rejected the studio’s bid to place “Michael” in the comedy or musical categories, a submission that came with a letter from Fuqua, pushing the film into the more crowded drama race. An FYC screening at the DGA reportedly drew a standing ovation.

At the Gotham Awards on Nov. 30, Fuqua, King, Jaafar Jackson, Colman Domingo and Nia Long will accept the Musical Tribute Award.

The commercial case was settled months ago, with a sequel currently in development.

“Michael” opened in April to $97 million domestically and $217 million worldwide, a record debut for a music biopic. In July, it became the first biopic to cross $1 billion globally. It’s Lionsgate’s biggest release ever, topping the $865 million of “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire” and the studio says it’s the first film from an independent distributor to reach the milestone. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The critics’ reception was much harsher than audiences’. The film currently holds a 38% score on Rotten Tomatoes. However, viewers have consistently singled out Jaafar Jackson’s star-making turn as his uncle; audiences gave it an A- CinemaScore.

Written by John Logan, “Michael” traces Jackson’s rise from the Jackson 5 in the 1960s through the Bad World Tour in the late 1980s, closing before the first allegations of misconduct became public in 1993. Jaafar Jackson leads a cast that includes Domingo as Joseph Jackson, Long as Katherine Jackson, Miles Teller as attorney John Branca and Mike Myers as record executive Walter Yetnikoff.

Skipping BAFTA doesn’t affect the film’s Oscar eligibility, and the Globes, Critics Choice Awards and guild circuits remain in play. But it gives up one of the season’s biggest televised platforms, along with one of the few chances for a breakout performance to reach an international voting body before Oscar nominations voting opens.

Whether the decision ultimately costs “Michael” a trip to the Oscars remains to be seen.

articles.title: 'Yellowjackets' Creators on Closing Their Survival Story, Killing Characters and Thoughts on Spinoffs: "This Was Meant to Be the Final End"
articles.summary: Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson hope to leave viewers satisfied when the fourth and final season of the Showtime hit releases its series finale: "We do feel like this closes the book, and I think that's important."
articles.content:
[This story contains mild spoilers from the premiere of Yellowjackets season four.]

The end is near for Yellowjackets . The fourth and final season of Showtime 's hit survival story has begun, and the weekly drop of final episodes will send viewers on a wild ride as they ruminate on life, death — and the meanings behind those bizarre post- Yellowjackets dreams. If it's any consolation, the creators have those dreams, too.

"Life just keeps getting wider, and the show has been part of that. It's been an expression of that width and an agent in creating that width," Bart Nickerson , chatting with his co-creator wife, Ashley Lyle , tells The Hollywood Reporter of the last near-decade making the hit Showtime series. The pair initially planned for five seasons, but when the Paramount renewed Yellowjackets for a fourth and final season, the creators pivoted. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories NEXT BIG THING Jasmin Savoy Brown Bids Farewell to 'Yellowjackets' and Finds Her Way to 'Hadestown' Lifestyle The Paramount+ Black Friday Deal Gets You Two Months for Less Than a Latte

"For us," says Lyle, "it was about storytelling momentum and, with the uncertainty of the industry right now, let's just finish a story if we can . We took a good, hard look at it. If we had felt like we couldn't get it done, we probably would have taken the chance. But it felt like we could."

What they deliver is what viewers have been waiting for when the survivors of the Yellowjackets plane crash that began the series are rescued and returned home in the season four premiere. Following the teens as they reassimilate into life in New Jersey — while learning how to live with the murders and cannibalistic acts they harbor; the things they did to survive those months in the wilderness — delivers a fascinating watch and full-circle return to where this story began. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Below, Lyle and Nickerson dive into making the final season and what to expect, including the pain of killing off characters while always knowing who would survive in the end. They also explain why they aren't interested in spinoffs — because they're ending the story with a period, not an ellipses: "We do feel like this closes the book, and I think that's important. I think that's part of the contract with the audience — that you're telling a complete story."

We have been waiting for this rescue season. When we spoke with you two way back in the beginning of all of this, in your heads, you had envisioned Yellowjackets as a five-season show, and here you are ending with four seasons.

How big of a pivot was this to wrap up the show earlier than you planned?

LYLE Ultimately, as we were breaking this season, we realized that it was workable. It came down to: Do we potentially overstay our welcome? Of course, when you're making television, there's always a risk that you will not get another season. So we realized at a certain point that there was a much more high-octane version of this season that could accomplish all the things that we really hoped to accomplish when we first conceived of the show.

Coming off of the third season, we always knew we wanted to get the girls back home. Then we always knew in the adult timeline that we wanted things to start turning in on itself amongst these women in their relationships. And it did feel like we had hit that pivot point at the end of season three. So we just ended up going full steam ahead; burden the hand. The ability to tell a complete story, to finish it on our own terms, is something we're incredibly grateful for. We hope everyone feels a sense of satisfaction with this final season. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Given the narrative of viewers dropping off after two seasons of a show, did you feel like season three was the hardest point to keep your audience, and did that affect what you wanted to do going into four?

BART NICKERSON To be honest, I didn't know that was a thing — that audiences drop after two season. I think, in some respect, through the entire run of the show, there is, as it turns out, a gift in being, tremendously insecure and scared. ( Laughs .) Every script we've ever written, even if we're just going to our writers group, you have so much of your personal self-worth and the quality of that script, you kind of live and die on every piece of feedback. Although it sounds insane, the stakes of making a season of television are almost a little intellectual — you don't ever stand in front of the audience and hear them reacting to your thing. Because the stakes are always so high, it wasn't about: How do we keep this going? Or: People didn't like this, how do we address that? At the end of the day, you just have to make the story you're trying to make for better or for worse. And some may say for worse! ( Laughs .)

LYLE I don't really understand the metrics of how they're counting viewership at this point. I'm not sure anybody does. I think they said season three was the most watched, but some of that, I'm sure, is people catching up on Netflix. For us, it was about storytelling momentum and, with the uncertainty of the industry right now, let's just finish a story if we can . And we took a good, hard look at it. If we had felt like we couldn't get it done, we probably would have taken the chance. But it felt like we could. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As the storytellers, you have a huge ensemble. So many stories to tell. What were some of the biggest challenges knowing that this was it? That you had a finite number of episodes left.

NICKERSON Yes, just that in and of itself [is the challenge]. We love television. We love telling television stories, and we love our characters and want them all to have a full, complete arc. Then there is the reality only having so many pages and so many minutes on screen. So it's about how to be as efficient as possible, and that has always been a challenge. We’ve always wanted each episode, each season, each scene to have a beginning, middle and an end. So it’s about, how do you tell these stories with efficiency but also arc? That has always been an incredible challenge.

Did it leave more things on the cutting room floor? Anything you can share now that didn’t work or make the show?

LYLE Not necessarily in a macro sense for this season. Every episode, we're always over time. We'll sit with the editors and pull out 10 seconds at a time to get it under 60 minutes. You're always cutting. That was the case in season one. That was the case in season two. Sometimes you go back and go, "Remember when that scene existed?" And the fact is that it was sort of telling you that it didn't need to be there. So I think the process kind of works itself out as you go.

Does it leave more room for spinoffs?

LYLE That's a question for Paramount Skydance! blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

NICKERSON Having one less season [I don’t think changes that], because we came to an end that was meant to be the final end. There are always ideas you haven't had yet. So, never say never. But there isn’t something where it's like, because we had one last season, we could come back and revisit that.

Do you two feel like you are closing the Yellowjackets book with this ending? No ideas for a tangent or a right turn in any way?

LYLE We do feel like this closes the book, and I think that's important. I think that's part of the contract with the audience — that you're telling a complete story. I suppose in this day and age, there's a never-say-never quality to this question, but at the same time, we wanted to tell a complete story. We wanted it to feel like the audience had been on the full ride. And hopefully, that there's a lot of emotional satisfaction in the resolution that we find.

NICKERSON At the end of the day, there's a level on which, if you're telling a story about survival, you're telling a story about death, and that means there has to be an end, because that's what you're confronting — the end-end. And, what does it mean when it's over? I don't think it would be possible to tell a satisfying ending if it didn't feel like the ending … of everything … ever. ( Laughs .)

You come out swinging with the season four premiere jumping right into the rescue timeline. You could have built your way up to it. Can you talk about why you wanted to lead with it, and fill in the gaps from the past as the season goes? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

LYLE That is a storytelling paradigm we've always been drawn to: not necessarily the “what happens” but the “why.” That was a big part of season one with the question of whether or not they engage in cannibalism. There were people who said, did you ever consider teasing that out? And we're like, “No.” We wanted to put it in the pilot, because to us, the most interesting thing wasn't whether or not they'd do it. It was, why did they do it? How did they get there? What is the context for it?

Similarly, with this season, it was a clearing of the decks, a reset in a way that could set up this season as a standalone season. And again, it wasn't if they get rescued, it's how and why , and what happens in the aftermath?

We would talk in the writers room, now that we've got four timelines or (let's just make things a little more complicated for ourselves!), in terms of post-rescue, pre-rescue and present day. And it felt like what happened in the interim between Natalie's distress call and them getting rescued could serve much more effectively as a little bit of mystery. Because to us, the more important emotional heartbeat of this season was going to be the post-rescue: how they were coping with and the different ways they would personally strategize how they would handle the reintegration. That was a much more interesting question for us at this point.

So much has happened to these characters over the course of the series, but it’s also been almost a decade since you two started developing this show. Do you feel like you also have grown with the show, in terms of how you wanted to end it and what you want to say in the end? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

NICKERSON Speaking for myself, yes, tremendously. It would be difficult for me to fully articulate what I mean, but so much of this story is a result of stuff that's been churned up and has continued to churned up. I always say the best compliment that people will give us about the show is, “I just started watching Yellowjackets . My dreams have been so messed up!” This idea that there is a deepness to the show.

I’ve had some bizarre dreams while watching these screeners!

NICKERSON ( Laughs .) That's been our life for nine years! Just weird dreams. ( Laughs .) I feel like life just keeps getting wider, and the show has been part of that. It's been an expression of that width and an agent in creating that width.

This show is about surviving and about death. There have been so many big deaths along the way. We still feel Juliette Lewis' exit and last season, you took so many of them away! Fans are always reacting. How much did you take the fans into account when you thought about who is going to survive this season?

LYLE We didn’t. I don't think we can, because, ultimately, if we were trying to please some segment of the audience, we're going to displease another. We have to write it for ourselves and use that as a guiding light and principle. It's a fool's errand to try to do fan service, especially when you're planning how to end a show.

Bassam Tariq was once attached to direct Marvel's  Blade  with Mahershala Ali , but eventually exited the project.

In a new interview, the Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother director reveals why he decided not to helm the superhero movie.

"Life's too short to make shit films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script," Tariq told The New Arab . "If we disagree, it's between them and me. It's quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build."

Tariq told the publication that he found it "funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script." What complicated things is trying to explain to actors who their characters and didn't want to disappoint them if they didn't live up to the expectations. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The silver lining in walking away from Blade and the film never getting made was that some of the costumes for Blade were eventually repurposed for Sinners .

articles.content:
The reason so many of us cried at “ Project Hail Mary ” has five legs, no face and a voice that belongs to James Ortiz . And he's so damn effective.

In April, Variety exclusively reported that Amazon MGM would submit Ortiz for best supporting actor at the 99th Academy Awards for his performance as Rocky. We’ve written plenty of consideration stories. None has produced what that one did: TikToks, Instagram Reels and a corner of film Twitter demanding, with real passion, that someone “get this adorable rock creature nominated for an Oscar immediately,” as Mike Sawicki of the “Mike, Mike and Oscar” YouTube channel and podcast put it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Beast in Me' Season 2 Casts Riley Keough, Lorelei Olivia Mote, Aaron Paul, Taip Ceman, Matthew James Thomas Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Russell Crowe Sci-Fi Thriller 'Bluefly' Adds 'Beast' Star Daniel MacPherson (EXCLUSIVE)

The groundswell even made it to NBC’s “Today,” where Carson Daly spotlighted it .

Months later, sitting in the Variety Awards Circuit Podcast studio, Ortiz still sounds like he’s processing all of it. “Did this actually happen?” he says with a wince. “It feels like it happened to somebody else two years ago.”

On this episode, Ortiz talks about bringing Rocky to life through his puppet artistry, from the eight weeks his team spent turning subtext into movement to the hours of reference footage that guided Framestore’s animators. He also lays out what he wants from Hollywood when it comes to recognizing and protecting puppetry work, why Phil Lord and Chris Miller’s set felt like “putting on a play in their parents’ garage” and the “Batman Forever” obsession that shaped him as a kid.

Lord and Miller’s adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel opened in March to $80.5 million domestically, a record for Amazon MGM and went on to gross more than $680 million worldwide, the non-franchise phenomenon the theatrical business had been praying for. At its center, opposite Ryan Gosling’s Ryland Grace, sits Rocky, the Eridian engineer built by Neal Scanlan’s creature shop and performed on set by Ortiz and a team of puppeteers he assembled. He was hired to operate the character. The voice was supposed to come later, from someone more famous. At the 11th hour, it was his. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Born in Albany and raised in Texas, the Puerto Rican and Italian artist trained classically at Purchase College and found puppetry when the acting jobs didn’t come. His first agent told him he wouldn’t work until he was 40. He turned 40 a couple of months before cameras rolled. Onstage, he won an Obie for “The Woodsman,” designed the puppets for Lincoln Center’s “The Skin of Our Teeth” and created Milky White, the scene-stealing cow of the 2022 Broadway revival of “Into the Woods.” “Project Hail Mary” is his first film.

What strikes me is how plainly he describes the work as acting. He breaks down a script the way he once broke down Prospero and Oberon. The only difference, he says, is that he funnels those choices “through an external shell.” That’s why the conversation around him matters.

We've had versions of this debate before, with Frank Oz's Yoda, Andy Serkis' Gollum and Zoe Saldaña in “Avatar.” Ortiz is eligible for both the Oscars and the Actor Awards, where SAG-AFTRA covers puppeteers. In theater, he points out, puppeteers are most often classified as crew.

He isn't campaigning for a trophy so much as for recognition of a craft. “The goal is to create a character that you get lost in,” he says. “But I think there's value in talking about the folks that made that.”

Excerpts from the episode, edited and condensed for clarity, are below.

The way we approached making that thing, even though it was my first film ever, felt, from what I understand, quite avant-garde. In a funny way, it felt like I was doing some downtown play every day. But I left every day going, “I don’t really know what we just made.” There was such an emphasis on crafting and improvising on the take that there were so many different versions of every single second of that film. So two years of waiting was pretty brutal.

I was so pleased and surprised when I got to see the final thing, especially when, at the 11th hour, I was told I was going to be the voice. And then the studio and the team said, “Why don’t we talk about this?” That’s a really unusual thing for suit performers and mocap and puppeteers.

My goal was always to be an actor. I went through this classical training program at Purchase, and it was all Shakespeare and Chekhov, all the things I’m still really passionate about. Then it’s that funny thing: What do you do with that information? How do you sell cereal? How do you do a bite and smile?

The first agent I signed with, in my early 20s, the ink was literally still wet on the contract, said, “You know, you’re not going to work until you’re 40.” And I turned 40 a couple of months before we started shooting “Hail Mary.” Isn’t that nuts? So maybe he was right. Who cares? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I was always drawn to painting and drawing and sculpting. My father was always engineering and tinkering and building things in the house. My mother is an academic, really literary and taught me about story structure. Long story short, all of those elements go directly into puppetry. I loved acting, performing, directing, engineering and fine art and it felt like I gamed the system by finding something where I didn’t have to pick one. When the acting gigs weren’t coming in, one thing accidentally led to another. I said, “Yeah, I can do that for this wacky downtown show for $200″ and it kick-started this thing.

It's become a way for me to play characters I would never, ever be cast as. That's the thing I found about puppetry: It ends up being the most freeing form of acting because I don't have to start from how you perceive me.

On any other role I’ve played, sans puppet, I would have ripped the script apart trying to figure out who this soul is. How do they think? How do they love? What are they terrified of? Then the exercise becomes how you funnel that through your human shell, physically and emotionally. The only difference with puppetry is that I’m funneling it through an external shell. I’m doing all of the homework.

My approach, maybe because I started as an actor, whether it was creating Milky White on Broadway or “The Skin of Our Teeth” for Lincoln Center or the operas I’m doing, was always: What do we want the audience to feel? The precision will come later. This is a tool to play a character that should not be played by a person. So let’s take advantage of it. Let’s not let it be pedestrian.

I was originally going to play the puppet entirely by myself on set. Then we saw the scale of it and how many legs he had. We knew that from the book, but seeing the puppet, I raised my hand and said, “Guys, I do a lot of ensemble puppetry and ensemble direction in my theatrical career. I would love to bring in other local puppet artists and build a team.” Not people who are just there to hold a leg. I needed to get them inside my head so we could play this character together.

For about eight weeks before we shot, we focused on how to use movement to express subtext. This is a character coming from a pretty traumatic 80 years alone in space. This character has never been alone before in their life. They’re a eusocial species, so they truly don’t know what it is to be solo. How does that existential pain manifest physically? That’s the delicious stuff. And I’m making it sound like we did a Bergman film. There was a lot of humor and silliness, but all of that has to come from something that feels grounded. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

This might sound a little crazy, but there is no such thing, especially on film, as an actor’s performance being entirely their own. There are costume people and other artists collaborating with them to create this character. The way the DP shoots you, the way the editor crafts it, that creates the final character.

After we wrapped, I got to see a cut and Phil and Chris asked, “Do you have any thoughts?” I said, “Well, I do. Are you sure?” I sent about seven or eight pages of notes about who Rocky is and how he moves, so the animators had more information and Framestore implemented that.

When you’re getting a puppet on camera, you’re focused on the frame. But if they need to go back later and add a CG counterpart, what are they basing it off of? So I gave them hours and hours of me and my team with a smaller puppet covered in dots, playing full scenes without any breaks. It was a chance to throw in every good idea or any bad idea I had left that we wouldn’t have been able to shoot on the day.

My team and I had worked out little bits of funny business. There's a moment when Rocky has an epiphany and runs from one place to the other, and he falls ass over teakettle down this ramp. That was something we did on the reference table. When he sits on the beach at the end, his little legs wrap around him like a cinnamon bun. One of my puppeteers said, “It's so cute. I'm desperate to find a way to put this in there.” I went, “Yes, this is it.” And they did it.

It's one of the few unions ever that recognizes puppetry as performance. Theatrically, there's actually no puppet representation, union-wise. Most of the time, puppeteers are considered crew and that means a variety of other things. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Generally, when there’s on-set puppetry in a Star Wars movie or some big-budget genre thing, it’s been storyboarded within an inch of its life. The puppeteer is brought in: Here’s page five of scene six, he takes three steps and he turns. OK, that’s lunch. It’s much more technical. Phil and Chris and Ryan and all the producers were never interested in that. Working with Phil and Chris was such a, I’m trying not to curse, a friggin’ gift. It felt like being in a writers’ room, a fluid pitch meeting.

I don't know if credit is the point, but I do think acknowledging the effort, acknowledging that C-3PO was actually Anthony Daniels, there's something to that. The goal of all of this is to create a character that you completely believe, so you don't think about the other things. But from an industry standpoint, there's going to be more genre storytelling, more characters we currently cannot imagine. How do we keep having these conversations? I have to keep giving flowers to Amazon MGM because they said this was such an unusual way of working, so why don't we talk about it?

He was such a touchstone for how we approached Rocky. I was of the age where I ate up all those “Lord of the Rings” docs and special features. There’s probably a two-hour doc just about Gollum. I logged it away years ago. He walked so I could run. I am standing on the shoulders of many giants. I did not invent anything. But sometimes it’s a huge gift that someone else came before you, and you can point at something and go, “Like this.”

It’s overwhelming. I can’t process any of it. Who knows if any of this conversation leads to more? I don’t even want to say awareness. It’s not like a disease. Get tested for rocks. But this art form has always been there. It’s always going to be there. Obviously, the goal is to create a character that you get lost in, but I think there’s value in talking about the folks that made that.

It's a collaborative art form. There's no version of it that happens by one person. Many singular people are on the poster at the end of the day, but that's why the credits are so long. Every single one of those people bled and sweat and cried and probably got a divorce while they were making this thing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As a kid, I was such a fan of “Batman Forever.” I was so nuts about Jim Carrey in that movie. It's a great film, but there's also a longer conversation there about the queer identity that I discovered in myself from that film, which is not rapid fire.

Oh, my God. Easy. I always run toward “Un-Break My Heart” by Toni Braxton, and occasionally, if we're feeling frisky, I might do “Orange Colored Sky” by Natalie Cole.

“This Rock and This Man: What an Adventure!” It's wordy, but I think it gets us there.

I can clap with one hand. That's going to sound disgusting, I know. It's pretty terrifying.

It's a childhood thing. Blue Bell is a Texas ice cream brand, and in the ’90s, they had a different formula for cookies and cream. It’s changed now, and I don’t like it, but the original, I really, really loved.

Probably my Apple Pencil, because I'm drawing all the time.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Showtime's Yellowjackets is retuning for its fourth and final season, which has some fairly-high stakes hanging over it. Like other mystery-based shows ( Lost, True Detective ), Yellowjackets has consistently kicked the proverbial can down the road when it comes to revealing the juiciest parts of the secrets that it's teased since Season 1. But now it's the final chapter of the story and its time to pay the tab, with real answers and resolutions.

So how has Yellowjackets done with landing the plane (…no pun)? Well, according to the Rotten Tomatoes score for Season 4, the show has just done an okay job settling things. Yellowjackets ' Final Season has the lowest Rotten Tomatoes critics' score of the entire series – but don't panic, because there hasn't been that much of a fall off.

At the time of writing this, Yellowjackets Season 4 has Rotten Tomatoes critics' score of 82%, with over twenty reviews submitted. That is indeed the lowest score for any season of the series, as you can see in the chart below:

So, Yellowjackets Season 4 seems to be pretty much in line with the critical view of Season 3. If you want to view it in a positive light: Season 4 has experienced the lowest rate of drop-off in terms of critical score. Unfortunately, this seems to cement the fact taht the overall impression of the show is one of diminishing returns, season over season. Yellowjackets Season 1 was a near-perfect (or perfect, according to its score) supernatural-mystery-darma, which actually looked like it could be a true successor to Lost . And yet, by Season 2, the show started to feel wildly uneven: the survival-horror-drama set in the past (with the younger cast of leads) quickly overtook the present day drama (with the older cast of leads), which has seemed to flounder more and more as the seasons have gone on.

The Final Season of Yellowjackets will finally reach the long-awaited middle point of the story , when the Yellowjackets soccer team were rescued from the wilderness and returned to society. That will bring both sides of the series together, and hopefully have them work in tandem to hammer home the core points and themes of the series.

"Season 4 is definitely a big improvement from Season 3, but it's disappointing that the standards are so low that this will define the season as "good" rather than "excellent" like in Season 1," writes Katie Doll of CBR . "There's no denying that Yellowjackets is disheveled at this point, attempting to wrap up what was originally five seasons into four. But it still cares about the evolution of its characters, and how they turn out will likely be the reason people will tune in for the final time."

Yellowjackets is airing on Showtime and streaming on Paramount+.

Lauren Neustadter , president of film and television at Reese Witherspoon 's Hello Sunshine , is set to step down from the company at the end of the year, the collaborators announced on Friday. articles.title: Melania Trump Stresses Humanitarian Efforts at Chic Premiere for Two-Episode Series Documentary Follow-Up
articles.summary: At a tight-security screening at New York's Lincoln Center Thursday night, the first lady's longtime collaborators celebrated how the Brett Ratner-helmed show allows her to tell her own story.
articles.content:
In late January, Amazon 's Brett Ratner -directed Melania documentary debuted at the Kennedy Center in Washington amid crowds of demonstrators in the wake of the fatal shootings by ICE agents of Alex Pretti and Renée Good in Minneapolis. The president had also sparked backlash for his efforts to overhaul the Kennedy Center, including adding his name to the exterior, which are still playing out in court.

Thursday night, Melania: The Series , a two-episode follow-up, though part of the initial $40 million project, consisting of bonus footage, debuted at New York's Lincoln Center. Those involved with the film and series downplayed any significance of the change in venue, noting the president and first lady's ties to New York. But if there were demonstrators, they weren't seen or heard by those inside the tight-security screening at Alice Tully Hall, though whether that's due to people moving on or the premiere location remains an open question. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Trump's $15 Billion Defamation Suit Against The New York Times Moves Forward TV CBS Inks New Deal to Air Kennedy Center Honors

The screening came just two weeks after the 2026 midterm elections saw Democrats score historic, surprise victories in a referendum on the president that will result in a change in party control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Still, Trump's longtime adviser Marc Beckman previously teased that the docuseries , now streaming on Amazon's Prime Video , would be a "total different experience, completely new."

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter ahead of the Melania: The Series premiere, Beckman explained how the filmmaking team determined what would go in the documentary and what would be for the series. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"We decided that we would bifurcate and isolate certain stories that we thought were suitable for the series that weren't necessarily appropriate for the film," Beckman said. "The reason they're suitable for the series is because it gives us more time to unpack more of her storyline, more about her family, more about her career, more about philanthropy and also what happens right after the inauguration when she takes on the role of being first lady of the United States again."

Melania: The Series producer Fernando Sulichin, who took on the same role on the documentary, added that the film "was about going into the inauguration, and this one is first lady in action and what she's about, more intimate — not the preparation of becoming the first lady but being the first lady."

Beckman likened the approach to what Trump's team did with her 2024 self-titled memoir Melania .

"With the trade edition of the book, we tell the story and we have certain photos in it, and then the collector's edition, it's a completely different experience so the fans could get both and enjoy them," he said. "That's the same thing here."

Though it was initially expected that the docuseries would arrive on Amazon's Prime Video when the documentary began streaming in March , Beckman said that was "just the media speculating," and insisted the timing of the series' release was in keeping with the licensing deal with Amazon he negotiated for the film and series.

"The timing for the contract is exactly what we've done," he told THR on the black carpet Thursday night. "I negotiated the contract, so trust me, there's no delay." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While the documentary film, which was released in theaters in late January, followed Trump in the two weeks leading up to the start of her husband's second term as president, the docuseries, in which Trump answers softball questions about her daily routine, interests and beliefs, first focuses on her role as a wife and mother, including her relationship with the president, followed by an episode centered around her and the president's trips to North Carolina in the wake of Hurricane Helene and Los Angeles after the 2025 wildfires.

The film, coming in the wake of Trump's best-selling memoir, was seen as part of a launch of a lifestyle brand . The doc and series' $40 million Amazon purchase sparked backlash that the tech giant was trying to curry favor with the White House, criticism likely to continue with the project's latest extension.

And while the Lincoln Center screening boasted Trump's signature black-and-white color palette, complete with a black carpet and white tables and flowers, as well as tickets and popcorn boxes featuring the first lady's face, Beckman steered questions about a possible lifestyle company back to Trump's humanitarian efforts, specifically her work brokering a ceasefire in Oleshky, Ukraine and her Fostering the Future initiative to provide resources and educational opportunities for foster kids.

"I think right now what she's really proud of is how she's helping children and people throughout the world," Beckman said. "What she's doing in America is so much more important than a lifestyle brand." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

And before the docuseries premiered, Trump spoke, from a black-and-white podium bearing her name, about the Ukraine ceasefire, connecting it to her own personal ethos and the series' focus, and episode titles, of "Family & Trust" and "Pride & Honor."

"We live in a world that never stops moving, but life's greatest moments belong to those who can stand still," she began. "In calmness, we can see beauty. In peace, we can see humanity. My work is demanding, and sometimes the challenges I face seem impossible. Still, even in the most difficult circumstances, I find the drive to achieve the impossible. I rely on my own strength and character, with conviction, courage and reckless determination. I found a way forward where others would not.”

"For a brief moment, the world stood still for Oleshky. Eight hundred lives were saved. After so many years of fighting, the ceasefire brought a little bit of sunshine into lives which had been in the shadows of fear and war. The moment was very powerful for me because fighting and conflict have no value to the families on either side. Peace is rational,” she continued. “In the Oleshky ceasefire, we see the power of family, the restoration of trust and the courage of young children who do not back down in the face of war. Family, trust, pride, honor are the values we all hold in our hearts; they are also the foundation of the personal story I'm going to share with you tonight as part of Melania: The Series ."

As Trump teased that the series offered the opportunity to "experience [her] world through a new lens," Trump's current and former colleagues said they hoped the show, like the documentary, let Trump tell her own story. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

President Trump's first-term adviser Kellyanne Conway said conceptually that the documentary and series were "so amazing."

"She's obviously a very private person who has a very public life and in my view a very positive impact and that story does not get told," Conway told THR . "And that's OK, so let her tell her own story."

Fashion designer Hervé Pierre, who created the first lady's inaugural gowns for the president's first and second ceremonies, added, "She's not mysterious, but she's not all over the media all the time and I think when she does something like she just did with [Russia and Ukraine], it's not, like, fluff. It's a very specific mission. So I think it's important. I hope we will discover something that we don't know about her. And I think sometimes it's better for her to [express something in her own words] than to have an interpretation of what she's doing. At least you have a direct line."

And what sort of things might viewers discover about Trump that they don't already know?

Pierre, who's long worked with the first lady, offered a couple of insights.

"She cries when she laughs," he said of her tendency to tear up at humorous moments. "She's very happy. I've worked with difficult women for 30 years in haute couture. She never, ever raised her voice or [had attitude]. She's always in a good mood — it's fascinating."

articles.title: 5 1980s Cartoon Theme Songs That Should Never Be Replaced Even for a Franchise Reboot
articles.summary: The secret to a really good cartoon theme song is making a tune that’s hard to forget, even years and years after the show itself was taken off the air. The 80's were especially prolific at creating opening themes that did way more than just open the credits. Instead, they got you in the mood, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The secret to a really good cartoon theme song is making a tune that’s hard to forget, even years and years after the show itself was taken off the air. The 80's were especially prolific at creating opening themes that did way more than just open the credits. Instead, they got you in the mood, set the tone of the show, and even gained as much popularity as the cartoon characters.

With the sheer number of beloved cartoons being rebooted, revived and resurrected of late, it's always tempting to mess with the music too. Sure, some would work, but there are certain songs that just shouldn't be changed. They belong to the series, and removing them or altering them in any way would be like changing the characters altogether or radically redesigning their personalities. These five '80s cartoon theme songs are so intrinsically associated with the series that, even in a franchise reboot, you should think twice about replacing them.

Led by Jerrica Benton, who used holography to change into the glamorous rock star Jem , she was part of the awesome band known as Jem and the Holograms . Other than putting on concerts for their fans, the group was busy battling the corrupt music industry and performing in concerts and dealing with trouble caused by the rivalry with The Misfits band. It was a riotous mix of music, style, adventure and friends, unlike many of the other shows from the 1980s.

And the theme song? Truly outrageous! It's one of those theme songs that makes you want to grab your microphone and pretend you're a headliner at some sell-out arena, even if the only audience is the family dog. The original theme, "Jem Theme," is so close to the show's pop-rock personality and I honestly would hate to hear a new singer modernize the music. One interesting fact about the show is that Jem's holographic cover was powered by Jerrica's father's super computer Synergy .

Adventures of the Gummi Bears featured a band of magic bears who occupied the secret kingdom of Gummi Glen, where they relied on their time-honored wisdom and Gummiberry Juice to keep the humans at bay. Zummi, Gruffi, Grammi, and Tummi were all in the house as the Disney series was filled with fantasy, laughs, and adventure. One of those series that just had a little extra something on Saturday morning.

And that theme song! I love that theme song. It's all peppy and bouncy and just makes me want to grin and giggle and launch into the bouncy dance of happiness, like I'm about to try the latest batch of Gummiberry Juice. Did you know that the theme song was sung by Joseph Williams, later of Toto? That's quite a musical pedigree for a cartoon about bouncing bears! Maybe the series will get another reboot someday, but I hope they keep the theme song. I don't care how hyper-clean the animation looks in the future, I want to hear that music start up and those bears start bouncing!

ThunderCats introduced viewers to Lion-O and the other refugees from Planet Thundera as they settled on Third Earth and faced off against the evil Mumm-Ra. With characters like Panthro, Cheetara, Tygra, and the ThunderKittens added to the action, fantasy, and array of wonderfully wicked bad guys, this series was built for kids to dream of their own magic swords, space bikes, and cat-people superhero gear.

But let's face it, the theme song is an adventure all on its own! The musical score is rich, melodious, and immediately makes me think of leading an army in a crusade, even if I'm just sitting around in my living room chowing down on a bag of potato chips. The opening of the series was written and orchestrated by Bernard Hoffer, who also did the music for a variety of other TV shows, helping define the series' classic epic tone. It is a song that would have you yelling "ThunderCats, ho!" at the top of your lungs at inappropriate times. On a related note, there is a live-action ThunderCats possibly in the works.

M.A.S.K. was always one of those crazy shows that was clearly made to get every kid on the block to beg their parents for a new toy. The cartoon was all about Matt Trakker and his agents, who fought against the bad guys of V.E.N.O.M. and their leader, Miles Mayhem. It all involved cool hats that turned into their masks and amazing vehicles that could transform into even more advanced forms of machinery.

And how could I forget that theme song! I love the sound of the opening because it is so energetic, high-tech, and futuristic. It's like the theme song is a high-speed machine that takes off and flies away to save the world and it just takes you along for the ride. Man, I'll always remember how that song was pure hype. Oh yeah, did I mention that M.A.S.K. is an acronym that stands for Mobile Armored Strike Kommand? Yeah, I definitely want that original music to come back if this franchise is rebooted again. None of this remixing for new generations crap!

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles follows Leonardo, Donatello, Raphael, and Michelangelo, four mutant turtles trained in ninjutsu by their rat sensei named Splinter. They live in the sewers of New York City and spend their days battling Shredder, the Foot Clan, and many other villains, while having a pizza or two. It was one of the most successful cartoon TV programs ever made and suddenly made the franchise a global hit.

Oh, man, Cowabunga! The first season's theme song is pretty much perfect, from that truly goofy (but no less cool) opening to the phenomenal lyrics that introduce each turtle. Every time I hear it, I sing along, and I can belt it out from memory without missing a beat. Wanna know a little secret? The theme was sung by the song's writers themselves, Chuck Lorre and Dennis C. Brown. And yes, that Chuck Lorre, the former TV sitcom and The Big Bang Theory producer. There have been multiple TMNT reboots since the original, and it's no surprise that none of them could come close in terms of popularity and style. Just give me this song, a pizza, and four turtles!

Which of these classic 1980s cartoon theme songs would you absolutely refuse to see replaced in a franchise reboot? Did we leave out another unforgettable opening that deserves to be protected? Share your thoughts and let us know in the comments below!

Austrian filmmaker Adrian Goiginger’s “Four Minus Three” emerged as the big winner at the 47th Cairo Intl. Film Festival, taking home three awards, including the Golden Pyramid for best film, as the festival wrapped its 10-day run in the Egyptian capital on Friday.

The Austrian-German drama, which follows a professional clown struggling to find hope after losing her family in a car accident, also earned best actress for Valerie Pachner and best supporting actor for Robert Stadlober. Franco-Moroccan filmmaker Nabil Ayouch (“Everybody Loves Touda”) headed the international competition jury. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Beast in Me' Season 2 Casts Riley Keough, Lorelei Olivia Mote, Aaron Paul, Taip Ceman, Matthew James Thomas Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Russell Crowe Sci-Fi Thriller 'Bluefly' Adds 'Beast' Star Daniel MacPherson (EXCLUSIVE)

French filmmaker Rudi Rosenberg took the Silver Pyramid for best director for “Words of Love,” while Egyptian filmmaker Ashgan El-Hamus received the Bronze Pyramid special jury prize for “Al Baraneya.” Moroccan filmmaker Laïla Marrakchi and screenwriter Delphine Agut won best screenplay for “Strawberries.” The Henry Barakat Award for best artistic contribution went to cinematographer Marius Panduru and production designer Hendrik Van Kets for the Belgian-Dutch-German co-production “Heysel 85,” which revisits the deadly 1985 Heysel Stadium disaster in Brussels. The film, directed by Teodora Ana Mihai, also won the FIPRESCI critics’ prize.

In the Horizons of Arab Cinema competition, Rania Rafei’s “The Day of Wrath: Tales from Tripoli,” a documentary tracing decades of political uprisings in Lebanon’s second-largest city, won best Arab film and the festival’s best documentary award.

Sara Shazli’s “Your Daughter,” a personal documentary exploring the Egyptian filmmaker’s complicated relationship with her mother, producer and filmmaker Marianne Khoury, received the Horizons special jury prize. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Naël Khleifi and Lisa Debauche’s “Summer Meadow,” which follows a Lebanese apprentice shepherdess living in isolation in the French Alps, collected three prizes, including the $10,000 best Arab feature film award and a shared creative achievement prize. Manal Issa also won best acting performance for the film, after previously winning the Pardo for Best Performance in Locarno’s Cineasti del Presente competition for the same role. Mohamed Zineddaine’s “Until Dawn” shared the creative achievement award.

In the Critics' Week section, Lorenzo Ferro and Lucas A. Vignale’s “The River Train,” an Argentine drama about a nine-year-old folk dancer who dreams of escaping his rural village for Buenos Aires, won best film. Azamat Shargyn’s “Before the Sun Rises in the West” received the special jury prize, while Ishtiyak Ahmad Zihad’s “The Blind Girl and an Elephant” earned a special mention.

In the short film competition, Lenti Liang’s “Our Secrets” won best short film, while Pranav Bhasin’s “We Were Here” received the special jury prize. Sabrine Khoury’s “A Tenderness” earned a special mention.

The Youssef Cherif Rizkallah Audience Award went to Egyptian director Ahmad Abdalla’s “BerleeN_,” an ensemble drama following three Arab residents of the German capital whose lives intersect over the course of a single day.

The closing ceremony at the Cairo Opera House also saw veteran Egyptian cinematographer Said Shimi receive the Golden Pyramid Lifetime Achievement Award.

Marking 50 years since its founding in 1976, this year’s festival presented 145 films from 64 countries, including 17 world premieres, five international premieres and 87 MENA premieres. The event drew 53,000 ticket sales, according to festival president Hussein Fahmy, up from approximately 45,000 last year.

The program included screenings of restored Egyptian classics, the new Cairo Kids section and masterclasses with filmmakers Matteo Garrone and international competition jury president Nabil Ayouch, who were both honored with Golden Pyramid Lifetime Achievement Awards at the festival’s opening ceremony.

The festival’s eighth Cairo Industry Days brought together filmmakers, producers and industry professionals for workshops, pitching sessions and discussions. Its 12th Cairo Film Connection featured 17 projects from 12 countries that competed for 53 awards with a combined value of $410,000, including cash grants, in-kind services and invitations to international industry platforms.

articles.title: OG Mormon Wives Star Mayci Neeley Had A Candid Reaction To Her Texts Being Shown In OC
articles.summary: Sometimes a text can cause a lot of drama.
articles.content:
The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County , on the 2026 TV schedule , only just debuted as the first spinoff, and immediately had its own drama. Funnily enough, the biggest drama of the season involved O.G. Mormon Wives star Mayci Neeley, who got dragged into the mix when older sister McCall DaPron clashed with some of the new cast members.

I’m sure we’ve all said things in a text in the heat of the moment, but Mayci’s words got out for all to see, leading her to realize her mistake in responding in the heat of the moment. She also expressed real regret for having made the statement at all. In a recent apology statement, she said:

Even though the text did make me look at Mayci a bit differently from the impression I’d gotten of her on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives , I also understand wanting to defend a family member and don’t blame her for having a strong reaction to feeling like her sister was being attacked. It all felt a bit middle school, and I’m certainly not making ay excuses for her over-the-top response, but the firsthand experience with some wild drama on her own reality TV series probably led Mayci to have a more heightened reaction than she might otherwise have had.

Largely because of Taylor Frankie Paul, we’ve become accustomed to Mormon Wives being synonymous with drama, especially with the chaos surrounding production of the original series. After the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette , custody issues with her children, and her announced departure, it immediately turned attention to the new spinoff and the drama in the OC . So, I’m glad that Mayci didn’t seem to waste any time in sharing such an honest reaction to her own behavior.

articles.summary: Two SNES-exclusive RPGs have been announced exclusively for the Nintendo Switch. They will be playable on the newer Nintendo console via backward compatibility, though. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Two SNES-exclusive RPGs have been announced exclusively for the Nintendo Switch . Right now, in addition to no word on the SNES games coming to PC, PlayStation, or Xbox, there is no word of the pair of RPGs coming to Nintendo Switch 2. They will be playable on the newer Nintendo console via backward compatibility, though. They won't be playable until March 18, 2027, though, because they won't be out until then. This is the release date for the pair of games, set to arrive together in a collection.

More precisely, Japanese developer Mebius has announced the Dual Orb Collection for the Nintendo Switch, which features Dual Orb: Seireiju Densetsu and its sequel Dual Orb II , originally made by Prism Kikaku for the SNES. The pair of 1993 and 1994 SNES games were Japan-exclusive back in the day, and this isn't changing. This new re-release has only been announced for Japan. To this end, there is no English localization, so while there are easy ways for those in the United States and elsewhere to get their hands on the collection, they won't be able to play it without know Japanese.

Unfortunately, there is no new trailer to accompany the announcement. There's also no word of either game is going to be modernized in any fashion. They aren't being remastered or anything fancy, but they could add new modern quality-of-life improvements and features. If they are, though, we don't know about it because nothing has been said about it.

Back in the 1990s, traditional JRPGs were dime a dozen in Japan, but they were rarer in the United States because most of them were never localized for Western releases. These two SNES exclusive RPGs are just a couple of examples of what was very common.

Do either of these games hold up in 2026, let alone in 2027? Well, it's hard to say because they have never been accessible in the West. Typically, traditional JRPGs from the 16-bit era hold up pretty well. They are obviously very rudimentary, but they are playable. That said, if you don't have nostalgia for this era of RPGs, it's not easy to travel back in time and visit it. The genre, perhaps more than any other genre, has advanced incredibly since then, not just visually, but in terms of design.

If this SNES nostalgia is not to your liking, the good news is there is lots of SNES nostalgia being sold at any given point. To this end, it was recently revealed that two fellow SNES-exclusive RPGs are also returning in 2027 .
