articles.content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “War,” which had its season finale on Nov. 19 on HBO and HBO Max in the U.S., and drops on Nov. 20 on Sky and NOW in the U.K.

Over eight episodes of “War,” actress Carla Duval ( Sienna Miller ) and tech bro Morgan Henderson ( Dominic West ) have been squabbling over the couple’s multibillion-dollar fortune as they prepare to part ways for good. The winners, of course, have been the lawyers.

The series centers around two law firms: the modern and fast-paced Taylor & Byrne, founded by Nicholas Taylor (James McArdle) and Serena Byrne (Phoebe Fox), and the stuffy, old-school Cathcarts & Sons, led by St. John Smallwood (Pip Torrens) and Beatrice Ubosi (Nina Sosanya).

If there’s bad blood between Duval and Henderson, relations between the lawyers are worse and bloodier still. Which is perhaps why, in a season finale twist, the divorcing couple decide to negotiate their own settlement amicably, and away from their scheming lawyers.

With Season 1 wrapped up, creator and showrunner George Kay sat down with Variety to talk about some of the real-life inspirations for the show, why he decided on that surprising ending and what we can expect from Season 2 , which will see Taylor & Byrne and Cathcarts return with a new case and new clients.

A little bit. Twenty years ago, I had a company that made a documentary series about divorce, and it was quite grim viewing, unsurprisingly. Especially because it was real people, and there was no charisma going on — ["War" director] Ben Taylor wasn't directing it, basically, and it wasn't Sienna and Dominic. So I remember having that at the back of my mind, thinking the thing we don't want here is to make this grim or bleak or anything. And in fact, one of the phrases that we came up with in the writers' room was that this divorce would be the world's most expensive couples’ therapy. Even though you don't physically stay married, you end up closer together.

You want to leave people feeling: “That was good. I liked hanging out with those people.” They were awful a lot of the time, but everyone's redeemable. And Carla and Morgan don't despise each other. They just drifted and drifted and drifted.

I wanted to end that story in Season 1, because I wanted him to find his home. And so that was always intended as a season-long story, and really wrapped around that is that thing of “Is it possible to be a good lawyer and a good person?” And I firmly think it is.

We're not going to extend the espionage thing. But with Johnny, it's a question of can you ever trust someone who's done that? Which I think is a relatable thing, whether that's your relationship or your workplace. If someone's done something really untrustworthy, can you ever trust them again? So that will linger, and become a big part of Johnny's story. But the other thing is, we wanted to find a similar character who's not at the upper echelons of a law firm to really get behind in Season 2. That is Emma Laird, who plays Molly [a junior lawyer at Taylor & Byrne]. We cast Emma, and I remember saying to her, "You're amazing. Just so you know, please come and do Molly in Season 1, because there's loads more coming in Season 2.”

Every season, I think it's worth having someone slightly more junior through which to see the whole thing through a prism of them.

We don't see her in Season 2. We have guest stars for each season. But we do have a world. So people [in “War”] don't use X; they use Zephyr. The whole thing keeps kind of bleeding into itself.

That was written with a writer called Toby Finlay, who's brilliant, and we talked about that a lot in the writers' room. If you can't arbitrate on a divorce, you'll go to litigation, and that's when it will go public, because it's not protected anymore. And what's fun about that is when you've got a kind of Morgan Henderson and a Carla Duval, and they are very much in the public eye, that scene triggers the going public of the whole thing. So we were always thinking we want this whole thing to blow up in public on chat shows around “The Milliner,” which is Sienna's film.

We wanted to put the camera behind the chat show host and the guest, because it's only when you go on stage, you suddenly get the on-stage eye-view of what it's like to be on a chat show. We're so familiar with Graham Norton or Fallon or whatever, seeing it from the front. We felt it was such a private thing to see it from the other side, and then you can hear the lights kind of cracking in the heat, you see the light obfuscating the audience and the pressure of that. She's such a talented actress, Sienna. She can do this thing of having a public smile, but with private worry in the eyes.

She was really great in terms of dealing with the script and talking to me about, “I don't think she’d quite say it like that,” and we would sit there together on set and tweak stuff. But never did we talk about the meta thing of Sienna Miller in the public glare. She was treating it as a proper part.

"Notting Hill" plays that much more for laughs with Rhys Ifans in his pants. But actually, I felt that [showed] the press physically bearing down on you.

I really wanted to use it as a way to pressurize Sienna, like that door might physically collapse on her. It was a quicker way into just seeing that the weight of the press attention was right there, so it's a little nod to “Notting Hill,” just in the sheer kind of [gasp] of opening the door. But it's not used for laughs.

Who was the guy that chased that woman down the corridor? It was awful.

I think it's more that sort of stuff happens in hotels, and there's CCTV in hotels. You're always looking in thrillers to find ways you could kind of revisit. So it wasn't trying to plug into any one particular incident.

I wanted to make it a bit different because — full disclosure — I didn't want Olivia Wilde to think we were just aping her experience. But also, I thought by distancing ourselves from it, we could make it even worse for Carla by putting it right in her biggest night, her biggest moment. This really is the culmination. She's on a career comeback at that point. She's been in some less good movies than “The Milliner,” if you can imagine, and so this was a really special night for her. So using that for dramatic effect felt good.

But the thing that I was really inspired by the Olivia Wilde thing was just how professional and upset she was at the same time. Like we're talking about Sienna's ability to [show] the pain it's caused, and then you see how she's painting on a smile quickly to get through it. And I really spotted that in Olivia Wilde's way of dealing with that in that moment, which I thought that just reflected very well on Olivia Wilde. So I was happy to be inspired by that because it's probably an awful moment in someone's life, and you've got to be choose the right way to kind of be inspired.

There were lots of fun names. The script editor came up with a brilliant list of films that are sort of mid-level Euro, kind of awards worthy, like “The Red Violinist of Marseille” and things like that, or you know, “The Harpist of Madrid.” But in the end, it was just “The Milliner.” We had this story that she was undercover in occupied Europe with a hat.

The thing we look for in the divorce [case] is to analyze the relationships of all the lawyers. And with the libel case, it's all about reputation. How our reputations are affecting us at work and what our work reputation means to us in life is a really cool thing to have exposed by a libel trial. So it's about playing those two things off against each other, and bringing in a few new characters and a few new bits of casting to make it believable that what we see as predominantly family lawyers can also have other people in their departments who have libel experience.

Nick Mohammed really comes through in Season 2, which was again part of our pledge to him. And there's a new hiring at Cathcarts, who starts to — not cause problems, but definitely shakes up the dynamic.

Tonally, it's adjacent but it's not exactly the same. And we want to have different aspects. It's a different album.

I'm actually looking the other way. I'm looking for the thing that affects people and then looking for the legal equivalent. It's the relationship stories that we've seen in movies or in our own lives that we really relate to on an emotional level, and then quickly scouring law to say, "Well, where is that felt?" So it's less with Walliams or Russell Brand. Like, I'm interested in how the justice system will treat those people, but I'm not using that for inspiration for drama because I don't know how it feels for anyone involved because I don't know it. So we're trying to start with the feeling.

articles.title: Superman Just Revived One of DC's Strangest Weapons, and Ben 10 Fans Should Take Notice
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Ben 10 is a juggernaut of a franchise. The concept of wearing a watch that allows the user to turn into practically any alien imaginable has captured the hearts and minds of kids around the world, but what not many know is that DC actually introduced a similar concept decades before Ben first shouted that […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Ben 10 is a juggernaut of a franchise. The concept of wearing a watch that allows the user to turn into practically any alien imaginable has captured the hearts and minds of kids around the world, but what not many know is that DC actually introduced a similar concept decades before Ben first shouted that it was hero time. The H-Dial is a device with a rotary-phone-like face. When the user types out the word H-E-R-O, they will magically transform into anyone from an infinite array of heroes , both established and original. It stands as one of DC's most powerful weapons, but a new version introduced has the wackiest side effect ever.

Introduced in Superman Unlimited #19, this new Hero Dial has the strange side effect of making the hero in question switch bodies with the user. This is an absolutely massive departure from the norm for this device, and gives us a few very important revelations. One is that there are definitely other Hero Dials out there in either the universe or the multiverse. Two, this might even be a drawback of the original that we have yet to see. We definitely need to dive into this, and also tackle the question of, with a new Ben 10 comic underway, what it would look like if these two iconic devices met.

The issue started with the alien, and perhaps other-dimensional, planet of Oculus, inhabited by a one-eyed, squid-like people. An Oculan supervillain attacked a city with a giant monster, even wearing his own version of Lex Luthor's battle suit, which forced one brave Oculan to use their H-Dial to transform into Superman . However, it would seem that this H-Dial differs from the original, as the Superman of the normal DC Earth found himself trapped in the Oculan's original form. It came at a pretty terrible time, too, given that he was helping Tomorrow Man stop a major bank robbery. Thankfully, Jon proved more than capable, and Superman was still heroic, even in his tentacled body. He eventually swapped back, the issue ending with the same thing happening to the Flash.

This was a fun little adventure meant mostly just to force Superman to watch how competent Jon was in the field. However, it does bring up a good question about how the H-Dial works. We know that it allows the user to transform into any hero from the multiverse, with the New 52 version retconning it so that the Dial stole these powers from various heroes temporarily. However, that was never mentioned in the newer incarnations, so it's unclear if this is still a drawback. Either way, the people never swapped forms before, which is a hilarious new addition to that lore that deserves further exploration. After all, if the H-Dial can steal the powers of heroes from alternate dimensions, then storylines about those heroes losing them at the wrong time practically write themselves.

If you look at Ben 10, especially its earlier concepts that had Ben transforming into superheroes instead of aliens, it'd be easy to say it drew inspiration from the H-Dial. However, according to creator Duncan Rouleau of Man of Action, the similarities are entirely coincidental. Season one and two art director Dave Johnson claimed that the show drew inspiration from it during the superhero stage, but the show was pitched as multiversal in nature before superheroes anyway, so it's truly impossible to know how much the H-Dial influenced what Ben 10 ultimately became, if at all.

Either way, the similarities are apparent, and with Dynamite's new Ben 10 (2026) series retelling the titular hero's earliest adventures in a much darker tone, it's only natural to ask what a potential crossover with the superheroes Ben definitely drew inspiration from could look like. The biggest question is, of course, Superman. He's the most famous alien in the world, and with Ben's ability to transform into any alien the Omnitrix can scan, there's no doubt that becoming a Kryptonian would be the first thing on his mind. A comic book battle between these two would be absolutely legendary, but if they did ever meet, it's way less likely that they'd fight.

It's far more likely that Superman and Ben would join forces to defeat a bigger threat, like Lex Luthor or Brainiac teaming with Vilgax for his technology, or something similar. The team-up I'd want to see more than anything is definitely Ben meeting Miguel and Summer, the two newest users of the H-Dial who make a fine parallel to Ben and Gwen. Ben and Miguel spam-transforming into different aliens and heroes in a fight filled to the brim with references and creativity would be absolutely insane to see, and definitely be a chance for any artist to flex their stuff in the most fun way imaginable. A crossover between DC and Ben 10 isn't anywhere near happening, but given how closely they parallel each other sometimes, it's not out of the question, either, and I'd love to see it happen.

Would you rather use the Omnitrix or the H-Dial? Let us know in the comments below!

"I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we've repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks," he wrote in the statement on Instagram . articles.title: Demon Slayer's Success Continues to Be a Problem for the Anime Industry
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Crunchyroll / Sony Pictures Entertainment The Demon Slayer franchise started a chain of events that is negatively affecting the anime industry in many ways, and most of them are bad. Demon Slayer became one of the first anime to produce a movie that adapted canon events from its original source material. Demon Slayer: Mugen Train adapted the Mugen Train arc […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Demon Slayer franchise started a chain of events that is negatively affecting the anime industry in many ways, and most of them are bad. Demon Slayer became one of the first anime to produce a movie that adapted canon events from its original source material. Demon Slayer: Mugen Train adapted the Mugen Train arc into an almost two-hour movie, becoming a massive success and drawing the attention that would eventually make the franchise one of the most popular anime in the industry. Following the success of Demon Slayer 's first movie, it was evident that many other anime would follow suit, essentially creating a culture of producing movies to adapt canon events.

One of the earliest franchises to follow this format, although it may have been a coincidence, was everyone's staple sports anime, Haikyuu!! . After producing four excellent seasons, the anime announced that it would adapt the remaining story through movies. In total, three movies were announced in 2020, but in the six years since then, only a single movie has been released. The second is set to arrive next year, while the final movie is still nowhere in sight, leaving fans uncertain about how the franchise will actually conclude its story. While Haikyuu!! is one example, 2026 has brought some of the biggest and worst changes to the anime industry for fans, and it could all be traced back to the success of Demon Slayer .

Producing ambitious projects that meet the standards of the big screen naturally requires more effort, meaning more resources and time are poured into them. While seeing these ambitious projects on the big screen is mesmerizing, it also comes at the cost of fans being forced to wait even longer. This is highlighted by none other than Demon Slayer 's decision to adapt its final arc into three separate movies . Considering how everything has been planned so far, it is evident that all three movies will take until at least early 2029 to be released. This means it will take around six years for the trilogy to conclude, whereas the anime could have adapted the entire arc into a single long season of around 24–25 episodes.

With three to four years of development, the final season could have been released across six months of weekly episodes, allowing fans to see the entire arc by late 2027 at the latest. More importantly, releasing the final arc as a complete season would have maintained the momentum and built even more excitement as fans experienced one epic episode after another. This is also what the latest movie implied, as the story would arguably have worked better in the standard anime episode format. Unfortunately, many other anime are following this trend, spreading out the wait for new content through movies, especially for popular franchises that fans want to see return as soon as possible. One such example is Solo Leveling , which is reportedly getting a new anime movie instead of a third season.

The second season was released in 2025, and it was only recently announced that the franchise would get a movie instead of a third season, adapting the next canon arc. Although it has no confirmed release window yet, it will likely take until late 2027 or 2028 to arrive. Meanwhile, this trend has also affected the biggest anime of all, One Piece , whose next movie is reportedly going to adapt a canon arc from the anime , something no one ever expected. This has left One Piece fans waiting even longer for the final arc to be adapted, especially following the anime's change in release schedule. It is clear that the aim behind adapting more anime into movies is to generate greater revenue and success, but the question remains: can every other anime meet the standards that Demon Slayer has set?

Demon Slayer 's box office success is extraordinary and something that may never be matched, even by a major franchise like One Piece . The problem is that the movies One Piece is producing come with a lot of context, especially if they adapt canon events, meaning new fans won't be able to watch them without prior knowledge of the story. In contrast, Demon Slayer had already established its audience with the success of its first season and movie, making it a global phenomenon that everyone wanted to see. In that regard, Solo Leveling 's upcoming movie is perhaps the only one that could come close. However, considering the controversy surrounding Solo Leveling , it may not achieve the same level of success.

Meanwhile, with other movies, such as Haikyuu!! 's upcoming film, which is arriving after years of waiting, fans may have lost some of the context, and its release might not attract a particularly large audience. Meanwhile, movies from newer franchises, such as The Eminence in Shadow, are a shot in the dark. Demon Slayer 's success in the movie industry was lightning in a bottle , and for other anime to achieve similar success, especially newer franchises following this movie format, it will now come down to blind luck. Unfortunately, this trend is only beginning and could continue for a long time unless the industry recognizes the flaws in this approach, which not only costs more money to produce but also forces fans to wait longer to watch their beloved anime.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Let me guess: you probably didn't know there was a censored version of Grand Theft Auto 6 , did you? Better yet, the question is: how could one possibly censor such a massive game? As it turns out, other regions, including Japan, have a version of the game that has been censored quite heavily. What's being censored, you might ask? According to shared images and videos online of the Japanese version of the game, violence and nudity have both been subject to limitations in the Eastern part of the world.

In fact, the nudity censorship has elicited humorous reactions from some, including shower scenes. Take this image, for example.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol pic.twitter.com/u8v0f0cqz0

How this is any better than the original (and more natural, I might add) version is anyone's guess. Still, the ratings boards in other regions have demands that must be met in order to achieve commercial status.

From a violence perspective, blood and gore are significantly scaled back. Dismemberment is also eliminated. However, according to Gamespark , it appears these censored elements in some regions can be toggled or adjusted in the settings. However, the Japanese version doesn't appear to have any adjustment option for Blood & Gore intensity. To add to this interesting debacle, the Japanese version of the game is said to have a full 1 GB smaller data package than the other versions. This has led to speculation that nearly 1 GB worth of content has been removed from the game in some capacity.

The Japanese 🇯🇵 build of GTA 6 comes with censored nudity and blood scenes compared to the international version. pic.twitter.com/MncPLzVm4Z

While this may be intriguing, it isn't surprising. Japan and other countries such as New Zealand and Australia have strict ratings systems that have notoriously resulted in some form of censorship for graphic and mature themes in the past. GTA 6 has a fair amount of nude content, including an entire nudist resort on the eastern side of Watson Bay. How the Japanese version might handle this little society is anybody's guess.

With GTA 6 out in the wild after years of anticipation, everyone has been eager to explore the far corners of Leonida. There are plenty of Easter eggs to track down, sites to see, and strip clubs to check out for those looking to experience Vice City's more risqué nightlife. And despite GTA 6 being fresh out of the oven, there's already talk of GTA 7 . For now, however, enjoy Vice City in all its glory.

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Getting the Remake Treatment, and Its Original N64 Release Is a Surprising Steal
articles.summary: November 2026 has already been a banger month for video games, and GTA 6 isn't even out yet. The main reason for that is Nintendo's remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. There really isn't much left to say about how impactful the the original game was to the industry, thanks to its […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google November 2026 has already been a banger month for video games, and GTA 6 isn't even out yet. The main reason for that is Nintendo 's remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . There really isn't much left to say about how impactful the the original game was to the industry, thanks to its sprawling open world of Hyrule Field, its iconic dungeons, and of course, the Z-targeting system which countless other games adapted as target locking. It should be no surprise that sealed first edition copies of the game go for hundreds of thousands of dollars, but it seems this particular copy of Ocarina of Time for the N64 is going for a significantly lesser amount on Heritage Auctions .

That being said, $33,000 is by no means a small amount. But, considering similarly graded standard release copies of the game have gone for over $200,000 in 2021, the price for this one is comparably a steal. But why is there such a massive gap between these two items, given that vintage games only become more valuable as years go by? They are both sealed 1998 USA standard editions for the N64, and both have been awarded a similar grade of 9.8 A++. The only difference I can find is that the earlier one was graded by WATA, while the one in question has been graded by PSA. Perhaps this would have made a difference if one was more reliable than the other, but they are essentially the same entity after an acquisition in 2021. My theory is that it was one of the last big items with the WATA branding on it, before it became PSA.

The collector's market is a strange place which take a lot of experience to understand, and even the name of the grading authority now carries great value when appraising an item. Regardless, this copy of Ocarina of Time is undoubtedly a great collectible for even the most casual gamer, and the price makes it one hell of a deal. This is compounded by the fact that the timing of this auction couldn't be any better. With the remake releasing earlier this month, the value of the original is bound to skyrocket, as market conditions usually dictate. This means whoever ends up with this copy will undoubtedly be able to flip it for way more than what they paid for it.

With only three days left for bidding to end (at the time of writing), it looks like someone is going to end up with a pot smashing deal. However, you never know when a bidding war may ensue, and seasoned bidders tend to play the long game and attack at the last moment for prized items like this one. Whoever ends up getting it, and however much they pay for it, one thing that can't be debated upon is how revolutionary Ocarina of Time was when it launched, and how beloved it has remained since then. Nintendo seldom does things without a good reason, and remaking one of the industry's favorite ever games is nothing short of a master stroke.

articles.title: 'I Play Rocky' Fact vs Fiction: Butkus the Dog, Bloody Knuckles and Stallone's Fight to Get 'Rocky' Made
articles.summary: The beloved classic “Rocky” premiered half a century ago this week. Five decades later, “I Play Rocky,” in theaters now, tells the story of how unknown writer and actor Sylvester Stallone shoulders his way into not just writing the script but playing the iconic lead role of boxer Rocky Balboa, culminating in a best picture […]
articles.content:
The beloved classic “ Rocky ” premiered half a century ago this week. Five decades later, “ I Play Rocky ,” in theaters now, tells the story of how unknown writer and actor Sylvester Stallone shoulders his way into not just writing the script but playing the iconic lead role of boxer Rocky Balboa, culminating in a best picture Oscar.

In the year 2026, is it really possible to go back in time and depict the making of “Rocky” with perfect accuracy? The unvarnished truth doesn’t always make for the best dramatic impact in a movie — and Stallone and the filmmaking team have told somewhat varying stories over the past 50 years. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Including the Original X-Men ‘Just Felt Right,’ Says Kevin Feige: It's a 'Fun Way to Culminate' 25 Years Abdul El-Sayed Mocks Trump and Ted Cruz's Cruel Rhetoric on 'The View,' Jokes He Wants 'Jihadist Leprechaun' Printed on a Hat

“I Play Rocky” effectively toes the line between hitting most of the events of the production with some degree of accuracy and buffing up others for the sake of more effective storytelling.

Here are some of the scenes that happened just as “I Play Rocky” depicts them — according to most participants — and a few others that use a healthy amount of dramatic license.

Did Stallone really write “Rocky” in three days and then turn down hundreds of thousands so he could star?

“I Play Rocky” shows Anthony Ippolito as Stallone marching into Robert Chartoff and Irwin Winkler’s office and playing hardball with the big Hollywood producers, hearing offers of more and more money to give up his starring role until the producers finally agree. The need for a tidy narrative leaves out several details, though, and makes Stallone seem like even more of a total unknown than he was at the time.

The real story was a bit more complicated and left out the pivotal role that talent agents typically play in Hollywood deal negotiations. Chris Rumar, the son of one of Stallone's early agents, Craig Rumar, said his dad and Rumar's agent partner Larry Kubik were integral to getting “Rocky” off the ground. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Since my dad died nine years ago, Mr. Stallone has been on sort of a tour about these inaccuracies about how ‘Rocky’ was put together,” Rumar tells Variety . “This time it was the triple whammy — we got the book, ‘The Steps,’ ‘I Play Rocky’ and the rerelease of ‘Rocky’ all within a month. He has been doing interviews with some of the biggest names in media and nobody challenges him.”

Kubik explained on the "Sexy Boomer" podcast that he and Rumar helped plant the seed for “Rocky” by introducing his friend, producer Gene Kirkwood, who had a deal with Chartoff and Winkler, to Stallone. Kirkwood and the agents first tried to set up Stallone’s script “Hell’s Kitchen” (which later became “Paradise Alley”), but Stallone had already sold it to another company and was trying to double-dip. So he went home and started work on another screenplay, influenced by a boxing match he had watched.

As seen in “I Play Rocky,” Stallone did work day and night for 72 hours to sketch out the basics of the script about an aspiring boxer, with his wife typing up his handwritten lines. But he didn't write a fully-formed screenplay that fast — he sketched out the first third or so of the story, then made dozens of revisions before it was ready to shoot.

The neophyte actor insisted on starring in the movie he wrote — an idea which seemed preposterous to the studio, which would have preferred James Caan, Nick Nolte or Ryan O'Neal. “We negotiated a deal, and in the first deal he got paid for the script,” Kubik said. “I was told by United Artists that Mike Medavoy loved the script. But he loves it for Jimmy Caan. So I said, ‘That is not going to happen.’”

As seen in “I Play Rocky,” United Artists reportedly did offer up to $250,000 if Stallone would step aside, but “Stallone held his ground,” Variety reported. Did he ever deliver the titular line “I play Rocky” to the producers during the discussion of who should star? It's not clear if anyone can remember.

Did Stallone really sell his bull mastiff Butkus for $40 when he was broke, and then buy him back?

In “I Play Rocky,” Stallone treasures the stray dog he found on the street during one of his lowest periods. After moving to Los Angeles, he's still struggling to make ends meet, and sadly decides to sell Butkus to a stranger who compliments the dog for some $40. As Stallone often recounts and as seen in “I Play Rocky,” when it comes time to shoot “Rocky,” Stallone wants Butkus to be in the movie, so he tracks down the new owner, who says his kids love the dog, and ends up having to offer him thousands of dollars (the story varies from $1,500 to $15,000) to buy him back. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Stallone has told a version of the Butkus story many times over the years, naming a man called "Little Jimmy" as the one who bought the dog when he was broke. Stallone implies Little Jimmy was a stranger he met in front of a 7-11, before he sold the "Rocky" script.

But Jimmy Gambina, a diminutive boxing trainer who worked on "Rocky," has a much different recollection of what happened. Gambina told “Going the Distance” author Mike Sielski that he dog-sat for Butkus during the movie's production, and then Stallone gave Gambina the dog after his son Sage was born because he saw how close they had become.

When it was time to shoot “Rocky II,” Stallone wanted the dog back so he could appear in the movie. Gambina says he told Stallone, “You come over and explain it to my son. If my son says it’s OK, I’ll let you have the dog back. But we’ve had the dog going on three years now, and we love the dog.” Gambina says the two had a falling-out sometime after Stallone insisted on taking the dog back.

Did Stallone break his knuckles on a frozen meat carcass at a Philadelphia meat packing facility during filming?

Many people think “Rocky” was shot all in Philadelphia. But only the iconic steps, Rocky's apartment and some other exteriors were captured in the City of Brotherly Love over a frenetic five-day period. “I Play Rocky” shows Stallone’s Rocky Balboa training with sides of beef at a Philly slaughterhouse, but the 1976 original was actually shot at Shamrock Meats in the L.A.-adjacent meat mecca of Vernon. The beef was frozen solid, though, and after Stallone pummeled the icy meat for eight hours straight, he ended up breaking a knuckle, so that part of the movie is accurate.

The ice skating rink where Rocky woos Adrian after hours was the Ice Capades Chalet in Santa Monica, Calif., which later became a Fred Segal store, while the climactic boxing match was filmed at the Olympic Auditorium and the L.A. Sports Arena.

“To help keep budget down, Kirkwood made arrangements for merchandising tie-ins to lure unpaid extras to the Sports Arena Monday. A foreign auto was to be raffled off, in exchange for a plug in the film, and other merchandise was to be given away at 15-minute intervals to keep the extras from leaving,” Variety reported during production. Extras were also given meals from Kentucky Fried Chicken, one background player recalled. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Adding to his injuries during filming, Stallone did break a rib during his final bout with Carl Weathers, while Weathers suffered a broken nose.

Did the studio really try to sabotage the production to get Stallone out as star?

Stallone pushed himself to run an estimated nine miles the first day of shooting and 11 the second, wearing Converse sneakers the whole time and giving himself a case of shin splints, according to the recent book “Going the Distance” about the making of “Rocky.” It’s not clear whether he was really told by doctors to stay off his feet for two weeks, as “I Play Rocky” shows.

But Kubik said that although the contract required a tight shooting schedule and budget, as well as giving producers the right to replace Stallone, it wouldn't have made much sense to get rid of him. “I knew if they were going to shoot half the movie with him, there was no way they were going to shoot for five days and then say we don’t like him,” said Kubik.

Stallone had a similar memory of the contract when talking to Howard Stern in 2005: “We have a 14-day thing where we can fire you any time and, more importantly, we can reduce it down to 900 grand, all in, and if you can do the thing in 30 days, OK. If not, it’s over.”

So although United Artists did write the contract with strict requirements in order to come in under budget, it wouldn’t have been in anyone’s interest to try to get Stallone to quit after shooting had already started.

Variety reported that director John Avildsen used numerous tactics to save money and come in under budget, including saving $200 by having Stallone provide voice work for three or four disguised voices issuing from bars and TV sets.

Did Stallone call his dad, Frank Stallone Sr., and ask him to appear in “Rocky?”

Sylvester Stallone had a difficult relationship with both his absentee mother and his abusive dad Frank Sr., who could never seem to show his approval no matter what Sly had accomplished. “I Play Rocky” shows him extending an olive branch by calling his dad and asking if he can play a small part as the man who rings the bell at the end of the boxing match. Is that how it really happened?

Not so much, Stallone recounts in his book “The Steps: A Memoir.” As he tells it, when he showed up on set to shoot a scene, Frank Sr. was already there waiting for him and insisted on being given a part. There was just one problem, Stallone says in his memoir: The part had already been cast. “There was no reasoning with him, so with apologies, I let go of the timekeeper,” he recalled. When it came time to shoot, Frank Jr. repeatedly missed his cue and didn't ring the bell, and the result was a “big Italian drama” of a fight, Stallone said .

articles.title: Searchlight Pictures Casting Head Yesi Ramirez Leaving Division Amid Restructuring
articles.summary: The ‘A Complete Unknown’ and ‘Moonlight’ casting director said in a statement that she will return to casting independently.
articles.content:
Yesi Ramirez, the head of casting for Searchlight Pictures , is departing the indie and specialty division after roughly six years.

The move comes amid a restructuring in the casting department at the Disney-owned division, which this year released films including Wild Horse Nine and Ready or Not 2: Here I Come , with Behemoth! and The Families Stone on the way.

In a statement, Ramirez said she would return to the world of independent casting after leaving the company. “I'll genuinely miss working alongside my Searchlight talented colleagues, many of whom have become dear friends. At the same time, I'm excited to return to independent casting, get back in the trenches with filmmakers, and be hands-on in discovering more talent and being creative,” she said. “It's a part of the work I've always loved, and I'm excited to get back to it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies 'The Odyssey' to Receive Ensemble Performance Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive) Music Searchlight Pictures Enters Merch Partnership With Universal Music's Bravado (Exclusive)

At Searchlight, Ramirez oversaw the selection of actors on projects spanning the Oscar winner The Eyes of Tammy Faye as well as The Menu , Fire Island, Ready or Not and Ready or Not 2 , Rental Family and Flamin’ Hot. She personally cast the Bob Dylan biopic A Complete Unknown , advocating in particular for Monica Barbaro to play Joan Baez — a role for which Barbaro later earned an Oscar nomination.

Ramirez also personally cast the titles Chevalier , See How They Run and The Families Stone .

Prior to Disney purchasing 20th Century Fox, Ramirez led casting for three different film banners at the company and served as the casting director on The Hate U Give and The Art of Racing in the Rain .

Across her 20-year career in casting, Ramirez has worked on projects as varied as Blood Diamond, 21 Jump Street and Magic Mike XXL . She notably cast Barry Jenkins’ Oscar winner Moonlight , which earned her a 2017 Artios Award from Casting Society.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Just Got Confusing After Marvel Confirms X-Men Deleted Scene Is Canon
articles.summary: Disney - Marvel Is Channing Tatum's Gambit in Avengers: Doomsday the same one from Deadpool & Wolverine? If you ask Marvel boss Kevin Feige, the answer is yes. Marvel fans were beyond excited when it was originally confirmed that Tatum would return as the card-throwing, Cajun hero for the new Avengers movie, as he quickly became a fan […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Is Channing Tatum's Gambit in Avengers: Doomsday the same one from Deadpool & Wolverine ? If you ask Marvel boss Kevin Feige, the answer is yes . Marvel fans were beyond excited when it was originally confirmed that Tatum would return as the card-throwing, Cajun hero for the new Avengers movie , as he quickly became a fan favorite during the 2024 X-Men film, and that was after failing to play the role years prior . Now, though, it seems like his presence is about to be pretty confusing.

Speaking with Empire , Kevin Feige addressed whether the characters were the same with a sly confirmation, revealing: “[In Deadpool & Wolverine ] we see Channing look up, with a little sparkle in his eye that maybe he could get out of the Void, and clearly he does.” For Marvel fans, this reveal by Feige might be confusing, because the last time that we actually saw Tatum's Gambit in the movie was when the titular heroes were escaping The Void , and Gambit appeared to be swallowed up by Alioth. He wasn't alone either, with X-23 (Dafne Keen), Blade (Wesley Snipes), and Elektra (Jennifer Garner), all seemingly dying at the same time. A deleted scene tells a different story , though, and Marvel just confirmed it's canon to Avengers: Doomsday .

Though Marvel fans who only saw Deadpool & Wolverine in the theater may not recall this moment that Feige is talking about, die-hards who follow every crumb of MCU lore know exactly what he's talking about. Roughly a month after it was released, Deadpool & Wolverine star Ryan Reynolds revealed this specific moment in a post online, showing off a scene that confirmed Tatum's Gambit not only survived the deadly events seen in The Void but had escaped. Reynolds later confirmed that "a version of the sequence" is in the movie, but is buried "on one of the monitors in the deep background of the TVA." That said, it begs two major questions.

*whispers* Marvel Sparkle Circle #DeadpoolAndWolverine ❤️💛 pic.twitter.com/TtuZ5jSAdL

The first question that this scene forces us to ponder is…who opened the portal for Gambit to escape from? Originally, the Sling Ring portal was opened in the film by Cassandra Nova, and since she gets ripped apart by the end of the movie, it's not her. Perhaps Deadpool himself saved Gambit from The Void, but this brings up the second major question: What the heck happened to X-23 , Blade, and Elektra? Deciding that a deleted scene is canon doesn't feel that out of left field for Marvel, even if they claim that the footage can be seen in the movie (one assumes it requires a microscope to witness), but it leaves a major hole open about the status of beloved Marvel superheroes in the process.

Perhaps a throwaway line in Avengers: Doomsday will settle this all, but given the magnitude of the storytelling and the sheer number of characters, Marvel is probably just expecting fans to go with it when they get in the theater. What do you think? Is it fine that Marvel decided a deleted scene was canon and we should all just go with it? Or is Marvel having its cajun cake and eating it too?

However, Atlus has shared a new strategy to reduce the time between mainline Persona games, primarily between Persona 6 when it comes […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the biggest consistencies in the Persona series is how long it takes for mainline titles to come out, with the nine year gap between Persona 5 and Persona 6 only growing. However, Atlus has shared a new strategy to reduce the time between mainline Persona games, primarily between Persona 6 when it comes out and an eventual Persona 7 . This could bring the franchise back to its Persona 3 or Persona 4 days, where it only took a couple of years to advance the series forward rather than taking huge breaks to release multiple spin-offs over the course of nearly a decade.

A developer interview with Persona series general producer Kazuhisa Wada discussed how the franchise is expanding overseas, talking to "SegaSammyMania" as part of a multi-part talk on the subject. Toward the end of the interview, Wada explains how Persona 6 isn't the endpoint of the series, and instead is more of a new process to turn the franchise into an even bigger IP. The "brainstorming of creative ideas and developments" for Persona 6 and beyond seems to be a big priority for Atlus, especially after the recent success of their last title — Metaphor: ReFantazio .

According to Wada, "We're [Atlus] taking various measures to ensure that fans won't have to wait as long for the next installment as in the past," indicating that Persona 7 could launch within a few years of Persona 6 's release. Currently, it is unclear what the release window of Persona 6 might be, but many player theorize that as more information comes out, the title could be a mid to late 2027 title. In the past, the launch of Persona 6 would mean that the game would be the center of all Persona content for several years, reflecting the long time between mainline entries that has become the franchise standard.

Atlus seems to be realizing that players might grow out of the target demographic for Persona games if it takes them nearly 10 years to come out, even if spin-offs keep one title's characters, setting, and themes alive. With excitement for Persona 6 being high due to its mysterious status, perhaps Atlus wants to keep the incoming audience by making the series progress without as much wait. Further comments by Wada say that "to improve development efficiency, we are strengthening collaboration between [internal] departments and improving the development process by utilizing management and sharing tools."

While this is very savvy business-speak, Wada is referring to the three internal studios that make up Atlus, including:

By consolidating resources between all three groups, the most talented creators on all Atlus teams can contribute their talent toward the best Persona games possible. Cooperation has always been present in these groups, but official shared work between them could accelerate production of Persona works fast. Wada went on to also say that "we place great importance on sharing core values in development," meaning that the best ideas from all departments are something Atlus shares between their projects. Some of those ideas and values were listed to be "taking initiative, understanding and helping each other, embracing change while enjoying it, and breaking through preconceived notions."

Shared values between teams for Persona 6 or Persona 7 could allow Atlus to have a singular focus on the series. This could not only let Persona 7 use some of the same game-making techniques and assets from Persona 6 's production, but also let developers stay familiar with what the series need to evolve. Wada continues the interview mentioned earlier by claiming "we can reduce inconsistencies in judgment and focus our efforts on what truly matters" and "we are reviewing the very mechanism of product creation, looking beyond just a single product to future development."

Through this newfound collaboration, which has honestly been within Atlus since the production of Metaphor: ReFantazio , Persona doesn't have to rely on one person to have a consistent vision either. Training young staff is obviously a part to this, but considering how many Persona team members have already worked hard with Studio Zero on Metaphor: ReFantazio , the environment of the studio couldn't be more geared toward cooperation. Perhaps this confidence in how the team has worked on successful games like Metaphor has inspired Atlus to commit to a smaller gap between Persona games, or in Wada's words, "as the overall level of the team rises, the level of the leaders will naturally rise as well."

Unlike the gap between Persona 4 and Persona 5 , Atlus isn't suffering the financial disaster of its parent company that threatens the survival of their IPs. As Wada talks about how "it's essential fore all staff members to have a high level of awareness and perspective," it's exciting to think about how the Persona series will have more staff and resources to reduce its notorious break between mainline games. While we know frustratingly few details about Persona 6 right now, the fact that Atlus is describing it as a series advancement rather than its end is promising for the franchise's biggest fans.

In the atmospheric suspense drama, a worldly teen challenges a strict boarding school's resident "holy" girl.

articles.title: I Didn't Think It Would Take A Doc To Get Amanda Seyfried On SNL, But I Love Her 'Sweet' Response
articles.summary: Let her eat cake.
articles.content:
Amanda Seyfried busted onto the Hollywood scene on soaps in the Noughties, but it was her role in Mean Girls in 2005 that made her a household name. Since then, she’s been in a ton of huge movie and TV roles including Les Miserablès , The Dropout , Big Love , Jennifer’s Body , Dear John , Mamma Mia! and The Housemaid . Not one of these roles led her to landing on the relatively rare list names to ever host SNL . That is, until You Can See Everything came around.

I mean "sweet" in the literal sense. While we know Seyfried can be funny ( it’s like she has ESPN or something ), she does seem a little nervous about taking the stage at Studio 8h, and asked her fans and pals to “send cake.”

If you are a fan of the actress, you may already know she’s a noted cake lover. She turned 40 during The Housemaid ’s promotional tour, and there were so many viral cake moments, including one where she pretty much murdered a cake with a knife. Yes, it was fittingly on brand.

Getting a cake on your birthday is kind of fun, but cake actually has a special place in the actress' heart. She talked about this love of cake with Harper’s Bazaar once, so it’s a real thing.

I’m genuinely excited for Amanda Seyfried to expand her abilities and to give the late night series a whirl. It's a special rite of passage for a lot of Hollywood, and hey, if she's good, maybe one day she'll even enter the coveted Five Timers Club ! Regardless, if you told me all this would have happened because of a literal documentary, I'm not sure I would have believed you.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 is now finally live around the globe. Arguably the most eagerly anticipated game in history, most who are playing GTA 6 are surely nowhere close to finishing it, as Rockstar's latest boasts hundreds of hours' worth of content to dig into . Despite this, some have already started to think ahead, specifically with Grand Theft Auto 7 and what it might end up looking like. And if you feel like it already might be a bit too early to look forward to GTA 7 , one of the key bosses in charge of the series would agree.

Speaking on TBPN , Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about Grand Theft Auto 7 and what it might have in store. While Rockstar's world in GTA 6 is drastically larger than anything else the studio has ever done , Zelnick was asked if the next entry in the series could take place around the entire globe rather than in one region. Rather than entertaining this idea at all, Zelnick kept the focus on GTA 6 , suggesting that they've not even begun to think even a little about GTA 7 .

"We at Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 on November 19th," Zelnick said. "Wait, let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19th. And you're asking a question about GTA 7 . I mean, guys, really?"

Jordi: "Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?" @StraussZelnick , the CEO behind GTA 6: "We went live with GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7." https://t.co/Up2ILZaP5t pic.twitter.com/3fgFISHqgy

You can't blame Zelnick for having this reaction for a number of reasons. Not only do those at Rockstar Games surely have no idea what Grand Theft Auto 7 might look like right now, but their work on GTA 6 has truly only just begun. While the single-player component of GTA 6 is live now, it's expected that a new version of GTA Online will come to the game in the future . This will give GTA 6 a live-service aspect that will continue to take up a good amount of Rockstar's focus in the years to come.

The good news with GTA 7 is that Rockstar should be able to continue going bigger and better than before with the next installment in the series. GTA 6 sales have already been confirmed to have topped 32 million units , with Rockstar and Take-Two having made nearly $4 billion on the first day of the game's launch. This makes GTA 6 the most successful entertainment release in history, and will undoubtedly give Rockstar plenty of resources at its disposal whenever it does decide to make the next Grand Theft Auto game.

How do you feel about GTA 6 based on what you may have played so far? And do you think there's still room for improvement with GTA 7 ? Let me know in the comments below.

The news arrives in the same week that Scott received five nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards, recognizing her sixth studio album, "To Whom This May Concern."

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Hunger Games movie franchise is returning to theaters this week with the prequel film Sunrise on the Reaping , which provides much deeper backstory and context for the original Hunger Games book (and film), as well as its sequel, Catching Fire . As the franchise comes full circle, the former stars of the original Hunger Games movie franchise (Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, Woody Harrelson) have been back in the spotlight. Hutcherson has been particularly interesting to hear from, as he is currently in the developmental pipeline over at DC Studios, where he is set to play the character Scott Free (aka Mister Miracle) in an upcoming adult animated series that's set for release in 2028.

Of course, there have been some pretty seismic shakeups over at DC Studios in the last few weeks: After Warner Bros. merged with Skydance, James Gunn and Peter Safran were asked to step down from the leadership position of DC Studios and were replaced by Jeremy Latcham. Rumors are swirling that DC Studios could got through a major change of creative direction, and that old plans may not still pan out.

If you don't already know, DC's Mister Miracle animated series will be an adaptation of writer Tom King and artist Mitch Gerads' Mister Miracle comic series, which for 12 issues from 2017-2019. The comic follows Scott Free/Mister Miracle, the universe's greatest escape artist, and his wife, the cosmic warrior Big Barda, as they try to live a domestic life on Earth, but find that the escalating war between their homeworlds of New Genesis and Apokolips demands their attention and action. However, Scott's nightmare past (adopted and raised by Apokolips' ruler, Darkseid) and deep doubts about his seemingly immortal life take him down a very dark path of mental health struggles, in addition ot the battles he has to fight as a dad and Mister Miracle.

Josh Hutcherson will play Scott Free/Mister Miracle, and Mackenzie Davis ( Terminator: Dark Fate ) will play Big Barda in the Mister Miracle animated series. While speaking with Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast , Hutcherson addressed his DCU role and confirmed that it won't just be a voice-acting performance: he is set to play Mister Miracle in live-action as well.

"This [ Mister Miracle ] was like a very extensive auditioning process," Hutcherson told Horowitz. "Because whoever plays them in the animated version will play them in the live-action version. So that's the plan. That's the track that we're trying to follow. Tom King, who wrote the comics, is phenomenal. He was our showrunner as well, so he knows it inside and out. He knows Scott Free/Mister Miracle inside and out. And getting to have Mackenzie Davis there with me as well, to play Big Barda. She was amazing. That was just such a great project."

Hutcherson made sure to let DC fans know that this isn't just another acting job: he bonded with the character in such a big way that it probably helped him land the job.

"Mister Miracle came around, and I read. All I had was a few of the scenes to do the audition. And it was such a cool character, and then I started getting into the comics and reading through those, and the world is amazing. What it talks about with mental health and all of that, I think, is something that's very special, and I'm honored to be Scott Free, and I can't wait," Hutcherson later added. "I think that Mr. Miracle is such a great character, such an amazing story… I can't wait for people to see the show."

Mister Miracle is expected to be released on HBO Max in 2028.
